history.heading: From fishing villages to British colony
paragraphs: Before British rule, Hong Kong was an area of fishing and farming villages on the southern coast of China, part of the Qing Empire. After the First Opium War, China ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain in 1842. Kowloon was added in 1860, and in 1898 Britain leased the New Territories for 99 years.

Hong Kong grew into a major trading port. Japan occupied it from 1941 to 1945. After 1949, refugees from mainland China swelled the population and brought capital and skills, helping Hong Kong become a manufacturing and later financial centre.

history.heading: Return to China
paragraphs: As the lease on the New Territories approached its end, Britain and China signed the 1984 Joint Declaration. On 1 July 1997, Hong Kong was handed over to China as a Special Administrative Region, under the principle of "one country, two systems", which promised a high degree of autonomy for 50 years.

Large protests took place in 2003, in the 2014 Umbrella Movement for universal suffrage, and in 2019 against an extradition bill. In 2020 Beijing imposed a National Security Law, after which many opposition figures were arrested, independent media closed and electoral rules were changed to ensure only "patriots" govern.

culture.heading: East meets West
paragraphs: Cantonese is the most widely spoken language, and both Chinese and English are official. Hong Kong blends Chinese traditions with British colonial influences. Buddhism, Taoism and ancestor worship are widely practised, along with Christianity.

Hong Kong cinema, with stars such as Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan and directors such as Wong Kar-wai, was hugely influential. Its food culture is renowned, including dim sum, roast meats, milk tea and cha chaan teng cafés. The skyline of Victoria Harbour is one of the world's most famous.

politics.heading: Special Administrative Region
paragraphs: Hong Kong has its own legal system based on common law, its own currency, and separate customs and immigration controls, while Beijing is responsible for defence and foreign affairs. The Chief Executive is chosen by an election committee dominated by pro-Beijing members.

Since 2020, the National Security Law and a 2024 local security law (Article 23) have greatly restricted political freedoms, and critics say "one country, two systems" has been eroded. Many residents have emigrated, especially to the United Kingdom.

economy.heading: Global financial centre
paragraphs: Hong Kong is one of the world's leading financial centres and a major port, gateway between mainland China and the world. Key sectors include finance, trade and logistics, professional services and tourism. It has low and simple taxes and is a free port.
The Hong Kong dollar is pegged to the US dollar. Housing is among the most expensive in the world. Hong Kong is increasingly integrated with the Greater Bay Area of southern China.
